scenarios.description: A curricular topic with no MINEDUCYT registry entry and no supplied Santillana photo (e.g. Lenguaje grade 4, this family's real confirmed gap) must return a non-None gap, never an empty-looking result indistinguishable from 'nothing needed.'
A second Santillana photo supplied for a subject/topic that already has one cached must accumulate (both retrievable afterward), never overwrite the first into oblivion.
A non-curricular topic (is_curricular=False) must skip MINEDUCYT and Santillana entirely and return a clean 'use general sources' result, distinguishable from a real gap.
scenarios.verification: tests/test_grounding.py::test_non_curricular_topic_skips_mineducyt_and_santillana_entirely, and the audit CLI's own test_reports_a_general_topic_with_no_gap.

scenarios.description: Invoking the skill's real entry-point command(s) with no explicit workspace override must never write family data inside this repo's own checkout.
scenarios.verification: Needs a live check once Plan 3's actual parent-facing entry-point commands exist to invoke with a default path and confirm where they write. This plan's functions all take an explicit workspace: Path argument with no built-in default, so there is no code path yet that could default into this repo, but there is also no entry-point command yet to exercise end-to-end.

scenarios.description: An open/free-response question must grade as None at every stage (grade_answer, score_exam, needs_review, aggregate_topic_results) -- never guessed True or False.

A still-ungraded (None) result must be tracked as 'pending' and excluded from the graded total entirely -- not counted toward total without counting toward correct, which would silently lower a topic's score before any review grade exists. Renamed from an earlier, inaccurate 'never inflates' claim: a fresh review caught that the original implementation could still deflate a score, which is exactly what this guarantee says can't happen.

A second exam (a different exam_id) taken for a subject must accumulate in the child's exam_history.json, never overwrite a prior exam's entry -- the longitudinal dashboard view depends on a real history existing. Re-scoring the *same* exam_id (e.g. after an open-response review) replaces its own entry instead of duplicating it.
A topic with too few questions (below the 2-question minimum) must classify as insufficient_data, never a false 'solid' or 'needs_work' off a single data point.
scenarios.verification: tests/test_report.py::test_too_few_questions_is_insufficient_data_regardless_of_score, and the gap_report sort test putting insufficient_data entries last.

scenarios.description: Found live by a fresh whole-branch review running the real self-grading script under node: a radio's .value is always a string, so comparing it against a Python bool via JSON.stringify never matched -- every true/false question graded wrong regardless of the answer given. Fixed by mapping the chosen radio back to a real boolean (and, for multiple_choice/single_select, back to the original typed option value via its index) before grading or exporting.
scenarios.verification: Manually verified live under node (ad hoc, not a committed test -- this repo stays Python-stdlib-only) against the real script extracted from render_exam_html's own output: a correct true_false answer in both directions, and a non-string-typed multiple_choice correct_answer, both now grade and export correctly. The architecture fix below (score_exam as sole authority) is what the committed suite actually pins.

scenarios.description: The exported results file's 'correct' field comes from a second, independent reimplementation of grading logic running in the browser, which drifted from grading.py in confirmed ways (the true/false bug above, and a number-vs-string multiple_choice mismatch). scripts/audit_exam.py's score subcommand now recomputes every answer via grading.score_exam from the raw given_answer values and ignores the page's own claim entirely, matching the plan's own stated architecture ('grading.py is the only place that decides').
scenarios.verification: tests/test_audit_exam.py::test_score_recomputes_correctness_from_grading_py_ignoring_the_pages_own_correct_field -- a results file that deliberately lies ('correct': false for two right answers) is shown to be ignored; the CLI reports the true, recomputed classification.

scenarios.description: A correct_answer whose shape doesn't match its question type (e.g. a bare string instead of a list for fill_in_blank) previously corrupted Python's own grading silently (iterating the string's characters) and crashed the live page's download button outright. make_question and render_exam_html (which loads raw JSON and never goes through make_question) now both validate the shape and raise loudly instead.
scenarios.verification: tests/test_exam_schema.py's four new MakeQuestionTests shape-validation cases, and tests/test_exam_page.py::test_rejects_a_mismatched_correct_answer_shape_even_for_a_raw_loaded_exam.

scenarios.description: A matching question's dropdown options were rendered in exactly the answer key's own order, so the correct choice for the n-th pair was always the n-th option -- and every select defaulted to its first option, so an untouched matching question graded as already correct. Options are now shuffled and every select starts on an empty, disabled placeholder.

A question's own text containing a literal '</script>' would prematurely close the embedded #exam-data JSON block. The embedded JSON now escapes '</' to the equivalent, still-valid JSON '<\/' -- json.loads round-trips it losslessly.

True/False, the download button, and the matching placeholder were hard-coded in English regardless of the exam's delivery language -- the spec requires delivery language to be a parameter, defaulting to Spanish for this family's actual use. render_exam_html now takes a language parameter (es/en label table, es default) and sets <html lang>.
